episodeTitle.en: How to become a category pirate | Christopher Lochhead (Author of Play Bigger, Niche Down, more)
episodeTitle.zh: 如何成为品类海盗 | 克里斯托弗·洛克黑德（《放大格局、深耕细分》等书作者）

guestBioOfficial.en: Christopher Lochhead is a 14-time #1 bestselling author, top podcaster, and former 3x public tech company CMO and has been an advisor to over 50 VC-backed tech startups. He is best known as a “godfather” of category design, and Adobe named his book Play Bigger one of “the five greatest marketing books of all time.” In this episode, we discuss:• What exactly category design is • The “Frame It, Name It, Claim It” framework
guestBioOfficial.zh: 克里斯托弗·洛克黑德是14次头号畅销书作家、顶级播客主，并曾担任三家上市科技公司的首席营销官，还为50多家风投支持的科技初创公司提供过咨询服务。他被誉为"品类设计教父"，Adobe将他的《放大格局》一书列为"史上五大营销书籍之一"。在本期节目中，我们将探讨：• 品类设计究竟是什么？ • "框定、命名、主张"框架

title.en: How to become a category pirate | Christopher Lochhead (Author of Play Bigger, Niche Down, more)
title.zh: 如何成为品类海盗 | 克里斯托弗·洛克黑德（《放大格局、深耕细分》等书作者）

summary.en: Christopher makes the case that legendary companies design new categories rather than compete in existing ones: in tech categories, one company captures ~two-thirds of the total value, so competing means fighting for the remaining 24%. He explains category design as framing, naming, and claiming a problem (not just shipping a "better" product), and warns the "better trap" (Threads, Amazon Fire Phone, Red Bull Cola) fails because problems create categories, not vice versa. Practical tools include backcasting (envision the future, then work backward), "reject the premise," strategic languaging (e.g., Otis's "vertical railway," Starbucks's new vocabulary, OpenAI's "LLM"), targeting super-consumers, and the lightning-strike model of marketing powered by word of mouth. He also argues positioning and "product market fit" are dangerously incremental mind-sets.
summary.zh: Christopher 提出论点：传奇公司设计新品类、而不是在已有品类里竞争——在科技品类里，一家公司拿走总价值约三分之二，所以竞争意味着为剩下 24% 打架。他把品类设计解释为框定、命名并主张一个问题（不只是发布一个"更好"的产品），并警告"更好"陷阱（Threads、Amazon Fire Phone、Red Bull Cola）会失败，因为问题造就品类，而非反过来。实用工具包括 backcasting（构想未来再倒推）、"reject the premise"、战略性语言化（如 Otis 的"垂直铁路"、星巴克的新词汇、OpenAI 的"LLM"）、瞄准超级消费者，以及由口碑驱动的闪电袭击营销模型。他还主张定位和"产品市场契合"是危险的渐进式思维。
